children.prompt: Use your protractor to draw an angle of $58^{\circ}$. Place markers at distances of $3\text{ cm}$, $5\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ from $O$ and draw perpendiculars as shown.

answer.short: A $58^{\circ}$ angle with perpendiculars at $3\text{ cm}$, $5\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ from $O$, as shown in the supplied diagram.
answer.worked: Draw a horizontal ray from $O$. Use a protractor to draw the second ray at $58^{\circ}$. Measure $3\text{ cm}$, $5\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ along the horizontal ray. At each marker, construct a perpendicular up to the sloping ray. Label the heights $h_1$, $h_2$ and $h_3$, respectively.

inlines.latex: h_1\approx4.8\text{ cm},\quad h_2\approx8.0\text{ cm}\text{ and }h_3\approx12.8\text{ cm}

answer.worked: Measure each perpendicular from the horizontal ray to the sloping ray. The approximate heights are $h_1\approx4.8\text{ cm}$, $h_2\approx8.0\text{ cm}$ and $h_3\approx12.8\text{ cm}$.

inlines.text: Now look at the ratio of the heights to the bases
These ratios are all (approximately) 1.6. The ratios are the same since the triangles are similar.

answer.short: All three ratios are approximately $1.6$ because the triangles are similar.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{h_1}{3}&\approx\frac{4.8}{3}=1.6\\\frac{h_2}{5}&\approx\frac{8.0}{5}=1.6\\\frac{h_3}{8}&\approx\frac{12.8}{8}=1.6\end{aligned}$$
The triangles are similar, so their corresponding height-to-base ratios are equal.
